topics.name: GRC Overview
topics.description: GRC positioning and framework, key terminology, and technical details.

introduction.overview: GRC Overview covers the fundamental concepts of Governance, Risk, and Compliance in ServiceNow, including the GRC framework positioning, key terminology (policies, controls, risks, audits), and technical architecture.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 12% of the CIS-RC exam. Questions focus on GRC terminology, the relationship between Policy, Risk, Compliance, and Audit Management, ServiceNow Store apps, and GRC framework components.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the GRC applications available on the ServiceNow Store. Know the key GRC terminology and how different applications interact. Master the technical architecture including tables and relationships.
introduction.examTips: All GRC applications are available from the ServiceNow Store and require entitlement verification. Know the difference between Policy Management, Compliance Management, Risk Management, and Audit Management purposes.

topics.name: Implementation Planning
topics.description: Use cases, implementation team and checklist, risk and compliance personas, groups and roles.

introduction.overview: Implementation Planning covers how to plan and execute GRC implementations, including understanding use cases, building implementation teams, and defining personas, groups, and roles.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 5% of the exam. Questions cover GRC use cases, implementation methodology, team composition, persona definitions, and role-based access configuration.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand common GRC use cases and implementation patterns. Know the key personas (Risk Manager, Compliance Manager, Auditor) and their responsibilities. Master role-based security configuration.
introduction.examTips: Implementation follows ServiceNow best practices. Key roles include sn_compliance.manager, sn_risk.manager, sn_audit.user. Know which roles have create, read, update, delete permissions.

topics.name: Entity Framework
topics.description: Entity scoping overview, entity type approach, entity class approach, and entity architecture.

introduction.overview: Entity Framework covers how GRC applications scope work to organizational entities, including the Entity Type approach (departments, locations) and Entity Class approach (custom classifications).
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 20% of the exam. Questions focus on entity scoping, the difference between Entity Type and Entity Class approaches, entity architecture, and how entities relate to policies, risks, and audits.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand how entities define the scope of GRC activities. Master the two approaches: Entity Type (leveraging existing tables like cmn_location) vs Entity Class (custom entity definitions). Know how inheritance works.
introduction.examTips: Entity scoping determines what organizational units policies, risks, and controls apply to. Entity inheritance allows child entities to inherit controls from parents. Know when to use Type vs Class approach.

topics.name: Policy and Compliance
topics.description: Policy and compliance record lifecycles, architecture, configuration, and supporting processes.

introduction.overview: Policy and Compliance Management covers how to create, manage, and enforce policies and compliance requirements, including policy lifecycles, control frameworks, control testing, and attestation.
introduction.whyItMatters: This is a major domain at 25% of the exam. Questions cover policy lifecycles, compliance requirements, control design, control testing, attestations, issues management, and the Compliance Manager dashboard.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the policy lifecycle from draft to published to retired. Know how controls are linked to policies and tested for compliance. Master attestation workflows and issue remediation processes.
introduction.examTips: Policies follow a lifecycle: Draft → Published → Retired. Controls have design effectiveness (documented properly) and operating effectiveness (working as intended). Attestations verify ongoing compliance.

topics.name: Risk and Advanced Risk
topics.description: Risk and advanced risk record lifecycles, architecture, and configuration.

introduction.overview: Risk Management covers identifying, assessing, and mitigating organizational risks, including risk registers, risk assessments, risk scoring, and advanced risk features like quantitative analysis.
introduction.whyItMatters: This is a major domain at 25% of the exam. Questions cover risk identification, risk assessment approaches (qualitative vs quantitative), risk scoring matrices, risk treatment, and risk monitoring.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the risk lifecycle from identification through treatment. Know the difference between qualitative (high/medium/low) and quantitative (monetary) risk assessment. Master risk scoring and treatment options.
introduction.examTips: Risk treatment options include Accept, Mitigate, Transfer, and Avoid. Risk scoring uses impact × likelihood. Advanced Risk Assessment (ARA) provides quantitative analysis with monetary values.

topics.name: Common Elements and Extended Capabilities
topics.description: Integrations, content packs, platform capabilities, regulatory change management, and continuous monitoring.

introduction.overview: Common Elements covers shared GRC functionality including integrations, content packs, Regulatory Change Management (RCM), continuous monitoring, and other platform capabilities.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 8% of the exam. Questions cover GRC integrations, content packs from ServiceNow Store, RCM for tracking regulatory changes, continuous monitoring with alert rules, and common GRC elements.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand how GRC integrates with other ServiceNow applications. Know how content packs provide pre-built frameworks. Master RCM for tracking regulatory changes and continuous monitoring configuration.
introduction.examTips: Content packs provide pre-built control frameworks (SOX, GDPR, etc.). RCM tracks external regulatory changes and their impact. Continuous monitoring uses alert rules to detect compliance violations.

topics.name: Audit and Advanced Audit
topics.description: Audit and advanced audit lifecycles, architecture, personas, groups, and roles.

introduction.overview: Audit Management covers the internal audit process including audit planning, engagement management, audit tasks, observations, and reporting. Advanced Audit adds resource planning and project integration.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 5% of the exam. Questions cover audit planning, engagement lifecycle, audit tasks, observations, audit reporting, and the Auditor Workspace.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the audit engagement lifecycle from planning to reporting. Know audit personas (Auditor, Audit Supervisor, Audit Manager) and their responsibilities. Master observation management and remediation.
introduction.examTips: Audit engagements follow a lifecycle: Planning → Fieldwork → Reporting → Closed. Observations capture audit findings. The Auditor Workspace provides a unified interface for audit activities.
